correctness.rationale: A vertex with at most one successor satisfies any Delta formula; if branching vertices are independent, every successor of a branching vertex satisfies Delta p, proving validity. Conversely, for an arc v->u between branching vertices, choose a second successor w of v and two successors a,b of u. Acyclicity of the simple underlying forest and the exclusion of reversed arcs guarantee that the successor sets of u and w are disjoint and do not intersect the successors of v: any collision would give a triangle or a four-cycle, or require an opposite arc on an already oriented edge. Set p constant on the successors of v and w but different on a and b. This gives a failure at v, including if w is a sink. For the census, a planted head when the parent sends into it is of type C or D; a planted tail sending to its parent is of type A or B_1. Incoming-child and outgoing-child sets at the planted vertex therefore contribute the exact stated factors: outgoing count at most 0 or 1 for A or C, at least 1 or 2 for B_1 or D; in the latter cases all children must be nonbranching, and the root contributes q. Separating labels by unordered sets gives the exponential factors. The true root has the zero-parent-outgoing states C+D; marking a root multiplies each n-vertex contribution by n. Each coefficient is uniquely determined from lower z powers. With zero branches the outdegree sum n-1 gives one sink and all edges point to it; Cayley gives n^(n-1), also correct at n=1. Two adjacent branching vertices require the endpoints plus three distinct additional neighbors, and at order five the unique possible shape has central degrees 2 and 3, with 5·4·3 choices and a unique invalid orientation for each. Independently, I enumerated parent maps toward label 0 and each orientation through order 7, evaluated both nested Delta formulas as full Boolean valuation masks, and tallied branching by exact outdegree. I separately expanded ordinary rational z-polynomials through order 9; the totals match, and the independent refined coefficients through order 7 agree at five q values (degree at most floor((n-1)/2)). This check reproduces the 60 invalid orientations at order five and all given polynomials. The frozen script compares its refined EGF to hard-coded values, not to branch counts freshly tallied by its own enumeration; this limits what its code alone establishes, but the independent tally supplies that check.
residual_risks: The finite enumeration does not extend the theorem to graphs with cycles, loops, or opposite arcs; the all-order forest result follows from the structural proof, not finite extrapolation.

evidence: The outward census has only the ordinary parent-to-child orientation state; the undirected forest census has only total degree. The new decomposition must allow both directions on each formal parent edge and enforce independent outdegree branching under either direction.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Outward orientation fixes each edge once the root is chosen, so it cannot cover valid orientations with several sources. An undirected total-degree restriction is also not equivalent: undirected adjacent vertices of degree at least three can have outdegree at most one by orienting everything toward a sink. The stronger underlying topology is therefore different, apart from the missing directional marks and multiplicities.

value.rationale: This is an exact labelled census for a naturally specified modal-validity class, not merely a rediscovered frame condition or a table of small orders. Tracking the branch count gives an invariant of all orientations, exposes exactly how the first modal failures arise, and provides an all-order scheme that can be used in probabilistic or asymptotic enumeration. The two directions of the planted parent edge encode information absent from the prior rooted outward census.
residual_risks: No asymptotic analysis or general enumeration over graphs with cycles is claimed.
